After returning to the area, the coworker saw the employee inside the cage with the door closed. The employer stated that the employee must have entered across the conveyer causing the robot to pick the employee up thinking he was a pallet. The employee was caught within the cage under a robotic arm and died from crushing injuries to his chest.

summary: At 1:30 a.m. on January 17, 2017, Employee #1 was operating a forklift, removing stacked and wrapped bag pallets from a pallet wrapper. A Fuji-Ace Mechanical Robot was used to load pallet bags onto wood pallets on a conveyor, which moved the loading stack to a pallet wrapper. When completed, the employee then moved the plasticized pallet to storage within the facility. The employee witnessed the robot arm that was feeding pallet bags onto the wood pallets on the conveyor, strike a pallet bag, loosening a hose on the robot hand and causing a mechanical issue that stopped the loading process. Employee #1 climbed onto the stopped conveyor and walked into the caged robot arm area to reconnect the loose hose on the robots hand. As he proceeded toward the hose, the robot arm engaged, striking Employee #1 in the chest area, and causing a broken sternum and 2 broken ribs. title: A Zoox robotaxi collided with a silver Nissan Murano on Las Vegas Boulevard near Four Seasons Drive on September 25, 2026, sending the Murano driver to a hospital with minor upper-body injuries.
location: Las Vegas Boulevard near Four Seasons Drive, Las Vegas, Nevada
summary: On the morning of September 25, 2026, a Zoox autonomous robotaxi and a silver Nissan Murano collided on southbound Las Vegas Boulevard near Four Seasons Drive on the Las Vegas Strip. The driver of the Nissan Murano was transported to a local hospital with minor upper-body injuries. Nevada Highway Patrol took over the investigation and temporarily closed several southbound lanes for towing and investigation before reopening them. Zoox confirmed it was aware of the crash and stated there were no passengers inside the robotaxi at the time of impact.

title: A Waymo autonomous vehicle (Jaguar I-Pace) was involved in a crash with other fixed object in Houston, TX, reported to NHTSA as minor w/ hospitalization
summary:
On September [XXX], 2026 at 8:39 PM CDT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Houston, Texas was in a collision involving a barrier wall on Interstate [XXX] at the [XXX] exit [XXX] offramp.

The Waymo AV was traveling southeastbound in autonomous mode, in the rightmost offramp lane on Interstate [XXX] at the [XXX], when an SUV traveling southeastbound in the third lane from the left on Interstate [XXX] changed lanes, entering the leftmost lane of the three offramp lanes at exit [XXX]. At the same time, a passenger car traveling southeastbound in the center of the three offramp lanes, changed lanes to the leftmost lane, and the right side of the SUV made contact with the left side of the passenger car. The passenger car was pushed southbound and spun clockwise across the center offramp lane and entered the rightmost lane, the Waymo AV's lane of travel. The Waymo AV slowed and maneuvered to the right to yield to the passenger car, and the test driver transitioned the Waymo AV into manual mode. The test driver continued to brake and maneuver the Waymo AV to the right towards the south barrier wall, and the front right side of the Waymo AV made contact with the south barrier wall. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was not engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The passenger car sustained damage. The driver of the Waymo AV was transported from the scene to a hospital for medical treatment with alleged minor injuries. 

Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 1 of Standing General Order 2021-01 because an individual involved was transported from the scene to a hospital for medical treatment. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

title: Cologne police seized a Unitree humanoid robot and investigated two suspects after the robot allegedly groped a 16-year-old girl during a livestreamed incident on October 10, 2026, according to Cologne Police.
summary: Shortly before midnight on October 10-11, 2026, a humanoid robot allegedly touched the buttocks of a 16-year-old girl and made thrusting movements against her on a busy street in Cologne, Germany, according to a Cologne Police statement. The robot's 16-year-old owner and a 19-year-old companion allegedly filmed and livestreamed the incident, police said. Police located the robot in the trunk of a nearby car, where the owner had allegedly placed it, and seized it along with the suspects' mobile phones. A criminal investigation was opened on suspicion of a sex-based insult under German law, with investigators examining whether the robot's movements were preprogrammed or remotely controlled in real time, according to Cologne Police spokesman Christoph Bermel.

title: Tesla Model S Autopilot crash in Key Largo on April 25, 2019 killed one person and seriously injured another, resulting in a $243 million jury verdict against Tesla now under appeal in the 11th Circuit.
summary: On April 25, 2019, the driver of a 2019 Tesla Model S with Autopilot engaged in Key Largo, Florida dropped his phone and bent down to retrieve it. The vehicle ran a stop sign and a flashing red light at approximately 62 mph and struck a parked Chevrolet Tahoe. A 22-year-old woman was killed and her boyfriend was severely injured. A Miami federal jury found Tesla 33% liable and awarded roughly $43 million in compensatory damages and $200 million in punitive damages against Tesla; Tesla has appealed to the 11th Circuit under case No. 26-10858.

title: Lawsuit filed against Intuitive Surgical and VA physicians alleging robotic surgery negligence led to the death of a patient on March 23, 2023.
location: Boston, Massachusetts (Jamaica Plains VA Medical Center) and Providence, Rhode Island (Providence VA Medical Center)
summary: A complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts on March 20, 2026 alleges that a patient underwent robotic surgery using the da Vinci Surgical System at the Jamaica Plains VA Medical Center on or around November 17, 2020. The suit names Intuitive Surgical, Inc. and three physicians as defendants alongside the United States of America, alleging medical negligence. As a result of the alleged negligence, the patient developed Stage IV metastatic carcinoma and peritoneal carcinomatosis and died on March 23, 2023. The plaintiffs are his wife and daughter, seeking damages under the Federal Tort Claims Act.

title: Globus Medical Excelsius GPS surgical robot allegedly malfunctioned during spinal surgery on January 16, 2025, causing misplaced pedicle screws and persistent neurological deficits in the patient, according to a federal lawsuit filed December 5, 2025.
location: Merit Health River Oaks, Mississippi, USA
summary: On January 16, 2025, a surgeon used a Globus Excelsius GPS surgical robot to perform lumbar spinal fusion surgery on a patient at Merit Health River Oaks in Mississippi. According to a complaint filed December 5, 2025 in the Southern District of Mississippi (Case 3:25-cv-00933), the surgeon told the patient after surgery that the robotic arm had malfunctioned and that the L5 right pedicle screw was drilled in the wrong location. The complaint further alleges that the surgeon later explained the device had rediagrammed itself on the L4 vertebra, causing her to misplace one screw and reposition it intraoperatively, and then rediagrammed itself again on the right side, causing the L5 right pedicle screw to be placed lower than she intended. The complaint alleges that following surgery the patient exhibited persistent right lower extremity neurological deficits including loss of foot flexion and movement. The lawsuit alleges medical malpractice against the surgeon and strict product liability against Globus Medical.

title: VA surgical robot procedure at Charleston VAMC resulted in compartment syndrome and permanent arm disability for a veteran in June 2024.
company: United States Department of Veterans Affairs
location: Ralph H. Johnson VA Medical Center, Charleston, South Carolina
summary: On June 13, 2024, a veteran underwent a robotic-assisted laparoscopic prostatectomy at the Ralph H. Johnson VAMC in Charleston, South Carolina. The surgery lasted approximately 8-9 hours, during which providers failed to monitor or address impaired circulation in his left arm. Upon waking, he was diagnosed with compartment syndrome requiring fasciotomy and additional procedures over two weeks. He subsequently suffered a bilateral pulmonary embolism and sustained permanent disability to his left arm. His wife filed suit alongside him under the Federal Tort Claims Act in December 2025.

title: A Robotic E-GYM Leg Press machine at a Montgomery, Alabama YMCA malfunctioned on October 31, 2023, allegedly forcefully compressing a user's knees into her chest and causing sacroiliac joint dysfunction, piriformis syndrome, and sciatic nerve involvement.
location: YMCA Bell Road facility, Montgomery, Alabama
summary: On October 31, 2023, a plaintiff was using a Robotic E-GYM Leg Press at the YMCA Bell Road facility in Montgomery, Alabama, when the machine allegedly malfunctioned and forcefully compressed her knees into her chest. She experienced debilitating lower back and hip pain the following morning and required assistance to leave the facility. She sought emergency treatment on November 4, 2023, with diagnoses including bulging lumbar disc and sciatica. She filed suit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado against E-GYM North America, Inc. on a product-liability theory and against YMCA of Greater Montgomery on a negligence theory.

title: Tesla Autopilot disengaged mid-curve on a rural road in Cocoa, Florida on December 3, 2025, causing a collision with a utility pole that seriously injured the front-seat passenger.
location: Cocoa, Florida (Rosa L. Jones Drive, Brevard County)
robot_model: Tesla Autopilot / FSD on 2024 Tesla Model 3
summary: On December 3, 2025, at approximately 2:14 p.m. EST, a front-seat passenger was riding in a 2024 Tesla Model 3 traveling on Rosa L. Jones Drive in Cocoa, Florida. The vehicle's Autopilot system transitioned from ACTIVE_NOMINAL to UNAVAILABLE mid-curve without warning, leaving the driver unable to regain control within 6.01 seconds. The vehicle struck a stationary utility pole at approximately 24 mph. The passenger sustained serious injuries including cervical spine damage, peripheral nerve damage, and soft tissue injuries, and subsequently filed a products liability lawsuit against Tesla in the Middle District of Florida.

title: Waymo recalled 3,791 robotaxis after an unoccupied vehicle drove into a flooded road in San Antonio, Texas, and was swept into a creek, a software flaw that let the cars enter standing water.
summary: Waymo issued a voluntary software recall filed with NHTSA for 3,791 robotaxis in May 2026 after an empty vehicle entered a flooded section of roadway in San Antonio and was swept into Salado Creek. The fix stops the vehicles from driving into standing water on higher-speed roads. No injuries were reported.

title: An iamo autonomous taxi struck a ground plate during a test drive in Dänikon, damaging the plate and two tires.
summary: Three days before the public launch of the iamo autonomous taxi pilot project in the Furttal region, a test vehicle drove through a 30 km/h zone in Danikon and failed to recognise a ground plate as an obstacle, running over it without input from the safety driver on board. The incident damaged the plate and both right-side tires of the Nissan prototype vehicle. The Swiss Federal Roads Office confirmed that the remaining fleet could continue operating safely. The software was analysed and adjusted following the incident.

title: Autonomous community bus 'Kurulin' in Fukaya, Saitama collided with a roadside fence and bus stop sign on 6 September 2026, causing property damage but no injuries.
summary: On 6 September 2026 at around 12:40 pm, the autonomous community bus 'Kurulin' operating on the 'Hokubu Shuttle + Kanko' route in Fukaya, Saitama drifted from its lane near Arai Post Office and struck a water-channel fence and a bus stop sign. No passengers were on board and none of the three occupants (one driver and two autonomous-driving assistants) were injured. The city suspended autonomous operation indefinitely pending safety checks. The city and Saitama Institute of Technology, which developed the vehicle's autonomous system, attributed the cause to a sensor malfunction. This was the second property-damage incident involving the same bus, following a kerb collision in January 2026.
